title: Support hours, channels and peak coverage
status_rationale: No customers, support organization, support contract terms or ticketing system exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Support is available during US business hours in all continental time zones for sponsor staff, with critical-severity coverage at all times. Channels include an in-product case system, email and phone, plus an out-of-band channel that works when the platform is down. Coverage increases in the final weeks of December according to a seasonal capacity plan. Echelon supports sponsor staff; donor-facing support is the sponsor's choice and Unbound provides tools for it.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-XIN-SVC-008 requires a seasonal capacity plan and surge playbook for live channels.
intended_practice: Define support offering before the first contract.
customer_statement: We have not yet defined a support offering because we have no customers. We plan business-hours support with continuous coverage for critical issues.

title: Severity definitions and response targets
status_rationale: No customers, support organization, support contract terms or ticketing system exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Four severity levels are defined with examples tied to customer consequence (Severity 1 includes inability to approve or release grants, suspected data exposure, or incorrect balances). Response targets are contractual (for example 30 minutes for Severity 1 at any hour) and resolution targets are stated as objectives. Performance is measured from ticket timestamps and reported monthly. Customer commitments made in support cases are recorded with owners and due times.
intended_practice: Draft severity matrix with the support offering.
customer_statement: We have not yet set severity levels or response targets. We plan contractual response times for critical issues.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Escalation, named contacts and coverage despite small team
status_rationale: Staffing is not established; a small team makes named backups for every escalation level a material open issue.
target_answer: Each customer has a named primary and backup contact and a documented escalation path to executive level; every level resolves to a reachable person with a named backup, enforced the same way control ownership is (owner plus backup always resolvable).
current_practice: Unknown. No support staff or escalation path documented.
intended_practice: Assign named contacts and backups per customer at onboarding.
customer_statement: We have not yet established an escalation path. As an early-stage company we will disclose staffing and backup arrangements during contracting.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)
open_questions: How many people will be available for customer support at launch, and who covers when the primary is unavailable?

title: Support access to customer data
status_rationale: No customers, support organization, support contract terms or ticketing system exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Support staff and support agents have no standing access to tenant data. Access requires a case-linked request approved by the customer, is limited in scope and time, is read-only unless the customer explicitly authorizes a specific change, and is logged with every action visible in the customer's access view. Support can never move money, change payees or change authority on a customer's behalf. Emergency access is two-person break-glass, limited to read and protective actions, auto-expiring within four hours and notified to the customer immediately.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-XIN-IAM-005 and CNV-PLT-007 specify break-glass limits.
intended_practice: Implement support access as a first-class authorization feature before production.
customer_statement: Our design gives support staff no standing access to customer data; access would require customer approval, be time-limited and be visible to the customer. Not yet built.
owner: Proposed: Security Lead (role not yet staffed)

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent vendor staff from viewing or changing our donors' data without our knowledge.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Insider snooping, unauthorized changes, or social engineering of support staff to redirect funds.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Typical answers cite background checks, confidentiality agreements and role-based access; support staff usually retain broad standing access that the customer cannot see.
challenge.legally_required: No specific rule for Echelon; GLBA safeguards and state privacy laws require customers to oversee service providers' access.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in bank and enterprise data protection addenda.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendor support logs in as admin.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Standing access is eliminated in scope; support cannot perform money or authority actions at all.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Authorization engine enforces customer approval, scope and expiry.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Every access is an event visible to the customer.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Customer-approved just-in-time access with customer-visible logs instead of reliance on staff screening.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If database administrators or infrastructure staff retain unmonitored paths to tenant data outside the application.
challenge.alternative_risks: Slower resolution when customers are slow to approve access.
supporting_arguments: Customer sees exactly what support did.
opposing_arguments: Infrastructure-level access remains and needs separate controls.

title: AI support agents
status_rationale: Unbound requirements describe contextual AI assistance (REQ-X-055) but no support agent exists.
target_answer: Where AI agents answer support questions, users are told they are interacting with AI, can reach a human at any point, and are routed to a human automatically for financial, security, accessibility-accommodation or complaint matters. Agents can read only public documentation and the requesting user's own authorized data, cannot take financial, authority or configuration actions, and their model and prompt versions are recorded per conversation. Support conversations are not used to train third-party models, and evaluation of accuracy and escalation behavior runs on a schedule.
intended_practice: Decide whether to use AI support agents; if so, build to this design.
customer_statement: We have not deployed AI support agents. If we do, we plan to disclose them, provide a path to a human, and prevent them from taking financial actions.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure automated support does not give wrong answers, leak data or take unauthorized actions, and that a human is reachable.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Donor misled about a deadline or deduction, data from another tenant disclosed, or account change made by a manipulated agent.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Disclaimers and 'AI may make mistakes' notices do little; questionnaires rarely ask what tools the agent can call.
challenge.legally_required: Partly: some US state laws and the EU AI Act impose disclosure duties for AI interacting with people; applicability to Echelon depends on deployment and jurisdiction.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Unauthorized actions are eliminated in scope by giving the agent no action tools; cross-tenant leakage is reduced by building context only from the requesting user's authorized data.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Tool allowlist and tenant-bound context construction.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-conversation version records and scheduled evaluations.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Read-only, tenant-bound agents with mandatory human routing for consequential topics.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partly; evaluation results can be shared, but behavior is probabilistic.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain; some sponsors will forbid AI support for donors.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If agents are later given action tools without equivalent authorization checks.
challenge.alternative_risks: Incorrect but confident answers remain possible within read-only scope.
opposing_arguments: Wrong information can still cause harm, such as a missed deduction deadline.
Donors may prefer human support regardless.

title: Problem management, case visibility and support workforce
status_rationale: No customers, support organization, support contract terms or ticketing system exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Recurring incidents are managed as problems with root cause and fix tracking; known errors and workarounds are published to affected customers. Customers see all their cases, history and commitments, and can export them. Support is provided by Echelon employees located in the United States unless a customer agrees otherwise; any subcontracted support is disclosed with its data access.
intended_practice: Select a case system integrated with Unbound's case kernel; decide support workforce model.
customer_statement: We have not yet established problem management or a support workforce. We plan to disclose where support is provided from and by whom.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)
